title: Polynomial-time proper learning of Poisson binomial distributions
formal: Is there a randomized proper learner which, given n≥1, rational \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and independent samples from an unknown sum of n independent Bernoulli variables, outputs with probability at least 2/3 a Poisson binomial distribution within total variation epsilon, using time and samples polynomial in \(\log(n+1)\) and \(1/\varepsilon\)?
definitions:
The unknown distribution P is that of \(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\) with independent variables satisfying Pr[X_i=1]=p_i for arbitrary real p_i∈[0,1]. Samples reveal only the sum, encoded in binary, not the individual summands. The learner knows n but not the p_i. It has no probability-evaluation or parameter oracle.

A proper output is a finite list of rational q_j∈[0,1] and positive binary multiplicities m_j with sum m_j=n; it represents the sum of independent Bernoulli variables with m_j copies of parameter q_j. Parameters zero and one are allowed. The learner need not recover the original summands. Total variation is \(\frac12\sum_{s=0}^n|P(s)-Q(s)|\). There are universal C,k such that the worst-case number of bit operations, random bits and samples is at most C(log(n+1)+1/epsilon+ell+1)^k, where ell is the binary encoding length of epsilon. Sample acquisition counts as one oracle call, and reading each sample counts toward bit time. Output length and all parameter precision count toward this bound. The success guarantee holds for every unknown P and uses the learner’s random bits and independent samples.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked learner and proofs of properness, success probability and polynomial bounds, or prove no such learner exists. A learner outputting an arbitrary discrete distribution or requiring n separate output parameters does not meet the compressed proper-output target.
context: Diakonikolas, Kane and Stewart obtain an almost-polynomial proper learner and a structural approximation by few distinct Bernoulli parameters. Their output model motivates multiplicity compression.
why: This asks whether the structural requirement on the output imposes more than polynomial learning cost.

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial-time proper learning of Poisson binomial distributions
import_provenance.original_statement: From samples of an unknown sum of n independent Bernoulli variables, can one learn to total-variation error ε in time polynomial in 1/ε and log n while outputting a Poisson binomial distribution, represented by distinct parameters and their multiplicities? The hypothesis need not recover the original Bernoulli parameters.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The cited algorithm has (1/ε)^{O(log log(1/ε))} dependence; non-proper learning is already polynomial-time.

context_blocks.text: Diakonikolas, Kane and Stewart obtain an almost-polynomial proper learner and a structural approximation by few distinct Bernoulli parameters. Their output model motivates multiplicity compression.

sentences: Samples reveal a sum of independent Bernoulli variables with unknown probabilities.
The hypothesis must itself be such a sum with the same number of summands.
Repeated probabilities are represented by binary multiplicities.
The target is polynomial time in reciprocal error and logarithmic size, at constant confidence.
Nearly polynomial proper-learning results do not yet give the requested polynomial dependence.
